title: Freya and the Protocol
premise: Paloma Vane smuggles forbidden memories between the two halves of humanity—the orbital Consensus and the surface-born Freeholds—whose cold war has kept cryosleep ships grounded for a generation. When the derelict freighter Meridian docks with a crew aged backward and a reactor countdown buried in their restored memories, Paloma realizes both governments knew the ship was coming and each plans to wake only its own people before the countdown triggers a system-wide pulse. Falling for Ilse, a de-aged Consensus navigator whose memories he's hired to restore, Paloma must smuggle the truth itself past both regimes. In the end he wakes the cryosleep bays indiscriminately—half of each world's chosen and condemned alike—and the countdown becomes, instead of a weapon, the first shared event humanity has witnessed together in forty years.
about_author: Theo Eriksen is a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade relaying messages between ships that were legally forbidden to speak to one another. He writes near-future fiction about the people who move information across borders that governments pretend don't exist.

chapters.title: Contraband of the Mind
chapters.summary: Paloma runs a memory-cache through orbital customs on the long route between the Consensus and the Freeholds, narrating in close third person. He hides a dying woman's wedding memories inside a shipment of seed patents. The beat is competence and loneliness: he's the best at staying invisible, and it's costing him everything human.

chapters.title: The Ship That Sailed Backward
chapters.summary: The Meridian docks unannounced at Paloma's waystation, its crew biologically twenty years younger than their service records. Ilse, the navigator, doesn't remember her own name until Paloma's smuggler rig replays it to her. The beat is uncanny wonder curdling into dread as Paloma realizes customs wants the crew erased, not debriefed.

chapters.title: Ilse, De-Aged
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV as she recovers fragments: the Meridian found something in deep space, a signal that rewrites cellular time, and her captain ordered it suppressed. She and Paloma grow close over restored memories—her wedding, her defection, her daughter she no longer remembers loving. The beat is intimacy built on borrowed past.

chapters.title: Two Governments, One Secret
chapters.summary: Paloma discovers both the Consensus and the Freeholds received the Meridian's distress call years ago and each built a cryosleep ark to wake only its own people when the countdown ends. His old handler offers him citizenship to stay silent. The beat is the seduction of belonging offered at the price of complicity.

chapters.title: What the Captain Ordered
chapters.summary: Ilse recovers the final memory: the captain didn't suppress the signal to protect humanity—he sold it to both governments, and the 'backward aging' was the crew's punishment for objecting. Ilse must choose between the loyalty she feels toward her dead captain and the truth Paloma needs. The beat is grief weaponized.

chapters.title: The Long Route, Blocked
chapters.summary: Customs seizes Paloma's rig and his cache; his network of clients is burned one by one as both regimes hunt the Meridian's data. An old rival offers extraction for Ilse alone. The beat is betrayal and scarcity—Paloma learns what his invisibility was actually for, and that it's over.

chapters.title: Countdown in the Ice
chapters.summary: Aboard the Meridian's derelict twin, Paloma and Ilse find the reactor already counting down: forty days until a pulse that will fry every unshielded mind in the system—unless the cryosleep arks are filled and launched. The beat is terrible clarity: the choice isn't whether to act, but who gets saved.

chapters.title: Which Half Wakes
chapters.summary: Both governments demand the arks' launch codes; each offers Paloma everything—pardon, wealth, Ilse's safety—if he hands the other side's bays to the pulse. Ilse, remembering her daughter at last, refuses to let anyone be ranked. The beat is love against duty, stated plainly and at gunpoint.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Manifest
chapters.summary: Climax: Paloma broadcasts the Meridian's full memory archive to every receiver in the system, then overrides the arks to wake a mixed manifest—chosen and condemned, Consensus and Freehold alike—while Ilse flies the Meridian into the pulse to widen its shadow. The beat is sacrifice as an act of justice outside the law.

chapters.title: First Shared Morning
chapters.summary: The pulse passes; the arks open on mixed crews who remember, together, everything both governments buried. Ilse survives in a de-aged body with a future she didn't expect, and Paloma—now the most visible man alive—chooses to stay and answer for what he woke. The beat is hard-won hope and accountability.
